Website decisions

Should you improve your website or start again?

A confusing page, a broken form and an ageing platform need different solutions. Find the problem before choosing the size of the project.

AP Tech Agency3 min read23 November 2026

In this guide

Name what is getting in the wayTry the tasks that matterSee what a focused change could solveKnow when a bigger change makes senseCompare the complete plans

Name what is getting in the way

If your website feels dated, first ask what is making it hard to use. Can customers understand your service, find a product and contact you? Can your team update the content without a struggle?

Write down each problem in plain language. This helps you decide which parts need attention and which still serve the business well.

Try the tasks that matter

Open the site on a phone and a larger screen. Find a service, read a product page, complete a form or work through an order. Note where you get stuck. Screenshots and a short list of steps give the team useful evidence to review.

See what a focused change could solve

When the structure and editing setup still fit your needs, a few improvements may be enough. Clearer service text, a simpler menu, a repaired form or a better product layout can each address a specific problem. Ask what needs to change and what should be checked afterward.

Know when a bigger change makes sense

A redesign becomes worth considering when the structure, visual style and main user journeys all need work. A rebuild may be needed if the current platform cannot support your requirements. Ask the team to connect each proposed change to a problem you have identified.

Compare the complete plans

Compare the cost, features, content work and time required for a focused update and a wider redesign. Include the practical details: product data, payment connections and the pages people already link to.

Plan for the work behind the pages too. Content may need moving, old links may need redirects and your team may need help learning a new editor. Those tasks belong in the proposal.

Choose the plan that fits your goals and the resources you can commit. Agree on the tasks visitors should be able to complete when the work is finished, and keep later ideas separate from the current project.

Turn an idea into a plan.

Tell us what you want to achieve and where you need help. Start with a few details in our project brief.
